summary: “The Wright Brothers' Martian Heir” is an interactive scrollytelling web experience developed by Team Aevum for the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge. Grounded in the neuro-narrative principles of Will Storr’s The Science of Storytelling, our project breathes life into the extraordinary journey of NASA’s Ingenuity Mars Helicopter.Our purpose is to bridge the gap between complex aerospace telemetry and young minds (ages 5–10). By blending cinematic third-person moments—from the breathtaking Sky Crane landing with "Mother" Perseverance—with intimate first-person Animism, we let Ingenuity tell its own story. Through warm illustrations, real JPL audio, and relatable childhood metaphors—a 1.8kg lunchbox body, a "yellow cheese slice" solar panel, and kayak-paddle blades spinning at 2,400RPM—children don't just read about Martian physics; they touch, hear, and help Ingenuity survive 90 Celsius nights.Why does this matter? Because Ingenuity is the ultimate underdog story. Once dismissed as an "unwelcome guest" built from a smartphone processor and given just 5 flights, it defied a 1% atmosphere to soar 72 times. Though its blades now lie broken at Valinor Hills, Ingenuity is not forgotten—reborn as a 20-year weather station, it stands waiting for the very children reading our story today to one day walk up and say hello.
details:
Project Overview & How It Works"The Wright Brother's Martian Heir" is an interactive web-based storytelling platform dedicated to NASA's Ingenuity Mars Helicopter—humanity's first aircraft to achieve powered, controlled flight on another planet. Accessible via a clean, immersive web interface, our project guides users through Ingenuity's historic journey on Mars, drawing a direct parallel between the Wright brothers' pioneering 1903 flight at Kitty Hawk and Ingenuity's groundbreaking missions in Jezero Crater (which famously carried a postage-stamp-sized piece of fabric from the original 1903 Wright Flyer). Users can scroll through an engaging visual narrative paired with interactive data points, mission milestones, and engineering insights.

Benefits & Intended Impact
Complex aerospace engineering data and planetary mission logs are often intimidating for students and the general public. Our project bridges this gap by transforming technical telemetry and mission history into an emotionally resonant, accessible digital story. By highlighting how a humble technology demonstration exceeded all expectations—completing 72 flights instead of the planned 5—we aim to inspire curiosity in STEM, celebrate human perseverance, and educate learners of all ages about the realities of extraterrestrial aerodynamics.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software

Frontend & Web Development: Built using modern web technologies (HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript) for responsive design, smooth scrolling animations, and cross-device compatibility.

Version Control & Deployment: Hosted and managed via GitHub (Carl3268/The-Wright-Brother-s-Martian-Heir) for collaborative coding and web deployment.

AI & Content Structuring: Leveraged Google Gemini to assist in synthesizing NASA mission archives, structuring the narrative arc, and refining the storytelling experience.

Creativity & Team Considerations
Rather than presenting a dry timeline of statistics, our creative approach frames Ingenuity as a true "heir" to the Wright brothers, weaving historical legacy with futuristic exploration. During development, our team carefully considered three main factors:

Scientific Accuracy vs. Accessibility: Balancing authentic aerodynamic challenges (such as flying in a Martian atmosphere with only 1% the density of Earth's) with engaging, easy-to-understand language.

User Experience (UX): Designing a lightweight, intuitive layout that keeps readers immersed in the Martian environment without overwhelming them with text.

Educational Value: Ensuring every section leaves the user with both a clear scientific takeaway and a sense of wonder about the future of aerial exploration on other worlds.
